correctness.rationale: The finite support cutoff and compression lemma bound all coordinate permutations by a single exact prefix packing LP. Reversal maps its maximizing prefix onto an admissible terminal Schreier block, forcing equality. Involution forces sharp two-sided distortion. Explicit admissible dyadic blocks and a feasible dyadic weight sequence give matching leading logarithmic bounds. Exact rational LP certificates for m<=13 and 726 supplementary subset tests were run; general validity is proved analytically.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General hereditary-family isometry classification and p-convexified isometry rigidity do not bound every non-isometric permutation with equality for reversal. No stronger theorem in inspected relevant sections implies the claim.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: If all infinite Schreier surjective isometries are diagonal, it follows only that nontrivial infinite-coordinate permutations are not surjective isometries. It does not force any precise finite operator norm, reversal optimality, or the logarithmic leading constant.

value.rationale: The quantitative extremal distortion for the full coordinate-permutation group is a natural refinement of Schreier isometry rigidity. It identifies a universal maximizing permutation, an exact smaller LP for every finite dimension, the maximal forward-and-inverse condition number, and a sharp leading coefficient for the logarithmic growth across all finite p; these statements are not just one arbitrary finite computation.
